intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding myelin protein zero (MPZ).

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding myelin protein zero (MPZ).
checks.evidence_quote: the identification of a mutation in the gene (MPZ) for protein zero (P0) associated with this phenotype are described
checks.explanation: The abstract links an MPZ mutation to congenital hypomyelination in one patient, but it does not state zygosity (heterozygous) and does not use the CHN2 designation.

paragraphs.text: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy. Onset is in early infancy, and features include distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severely slowed nerve conduction velocities (Mandich et al., 1999). Sural nerve biopsy shows nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons with basal lamina onion bulbs and no myelin breakdown products (Kochanski et al., 2004). Smit et al. (2008) noted that most of the few patients described in the literature died within the first years of life.

paragraphs.text: Smit et al. (2008) reported a long-term follow-up study of a family in which congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy affected 2 generations. The disorder is characterized by onset of hypotonia, paresis, and areflexia before birth, in the neonatal period, or in early infancy. On histopathology, myelin sheaths are absent or thin.

paragraphs.text: Mandich et al. (1999) and Szigeti et al. (2003) found de novo MPZ mutations in patients with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy. Smit et al. (2008) found a heterozygous MPZ mutation in affected members of 2 generations of a family, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance. Kochanski et al. (2004) stated that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy can be inherited as either an autosomal dominant or an autosomal recessive trait.

paragraphs.text: Warner et al. (1996) identified 5 novel mutations in the MPZ gene in patients with CMT1B, DSS, or congenital hypomyelination. They suggested that these disorders may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities but may instead form a spectrum of related 'myelinopathies' caused by an underlying defect in myelination. They hypothesized that the differences in clinical severity among MPZ mutations depend on the type of mutation and its effect on protein function, that is, loss of function versus dominant-negative effect.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with congenital hypomyelination, Szigeti et al. (2003) identified a complex de novo mutation in the MPZ gene. The mutation was a 3-bp deletion of CTA at nucleotides 550 to 552 combined with an insertion of G at nucleotide 550. By conceptual translation, it was predicted to cause a frameshift.
